summary: This is a market-wide six-week radar, not a portfolio brief. The highest-impact chain is mega-cap earnings at the end of July, the GLP-1 leaders on August 5, Walmart's consumer read on August 20, NVIDIA on August 26, Jackson Hole on August 27–29, and the August jobs report on September 4.

events.title: Federal Reserve rate decision and press conference
events.implication: The decision sets the discount-rate backdrop for the entire six-week window and lands hours before the first mega-cap earnings cluster. Rates, banks, high-duration technology, and housing-sensitive stocks can all reprice together.
events.direction: Hawkish guidance is bearish duration and bonds; a dovish read is supportive unless the shift reflects a sharp growth scare.
events.magnitude: No single-stock percentage is defensible for a macro event. Use the 2-year yield, TLT, QQQ, and breadth to measure the actual shock.
events.action: Record the statement, vote, and Powell's inflation/growth language before interpreting same-day earnings reactions.
events.invalidation: A fully expected decision with unchanged guidance and a muted rates response.
events.watch: 2-year Treasury yield, QQQ versus XLF, TLT, and whether the first 30-minute move holds.

events.title: Microsoft, Meta, Apple, and Amazon earnings cluster
events.implication: Four index heavyweights report inside roughly 25 hours. Their cloud growth, AI capex, ad demand, consumer spending, and device commentary can reset expectations across software, semiconductors, digital ads, and e-commerce.
events.direction: Bullish if cloud and ad growth absorb AI spending while margins and guidance hold; bearish if capex rises faster than monetization or consumer/device demand softens.
events.magnitude: A single basket move is not defensible because each stock has a separate earnings distribution. Treat cross-company agreement as the market signal, not the first headline beat.
events.action: Build one comparison sheet: Azure/AWS growth, Meta ad pricing and capex, Apple services and device demand, and each company's forward capex/margin guidance.
events.invalidation: Mixed reports with company-specific moves and no common signal in QQQ, cloud, ads, or semiconductors.
events.watch: Whether all four point the same way on AI returns, data-center capacity, and consumer demand; disagreement means less index-level information.

events.title: Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly report on the same morning
events.implication: The two GLP-1 leaders can reset obesity-drug demand, pricing, supply, oral-drug expectations, and the competitive outlook for biotech, pharmacies, medtech, and telehealth names.
events.direction: Bullish on durable volume, improving supply, strong next-generation data, and pricing discipline; bearish on share loss, weaker persistence, reimbursement pressure, or capacity bottlenecks.
events.magnitude: At July 24 marks, the August 7 $1,200 LLY straddle implied about ±8.3% and the August 7 $49 NVO straddle about ±8.6%. Both are indicative midpoint estimates, not executable fills.
events.action: Compare volumes, price/mix, manufacturing capacity, oral and next-generation pipeline timing, and management commentary on compounding and reimbursement.
events.invalidation: Company-specific noise with no shared read-through on category growth, supply, or pricing.
events.watch: LLY versus NVO relative performance and whether HIMS, XLV, and XBI confirm the category signal.

events.title: July Consumer Price Index
events.implication: This is the first major inflation check after the July FOMC meeting and can rapidly reprice September policy odds across equities, bonds, banks, housing, and rate-sensitive growth stocks.
events.direction: Hot core inflation is bearish duration; cooler inflation is supportive unless it arrives with a sharp growth scare.
events.magnitude: Macro event; no unsupported ticker-specific percentage is assigned.
events.action: Compare headline, core, shelter, and services inflation with the 2-year yield and market breadth.
events.invalidation: A near-consensus print with offsetting components and little change in September rate odds.
events.watch: 2-year yield, TLT, QQQ/SPY breadth, and rate-sensitive sector leadership.

events.title: Walmart Q2 FY2027 earnings
events.implication: Walmart is the cleanest large-cap read on value-seeking behavior, grocery inflation, general merchandise demand, e-commerce economics, and the health of the mass-market consumer.
events.direction: Bullish retail if traffic, discretionary mix, e-commerce margins, and guidance improve; bearish if shoppers trade down harder, general merchandise weakens, or margin pressure returns.
events.magnitude: No option-implied move is published here; the date is confirmed by the earnings calendar, but the official event page was not yet indexed.
events.action: Compare traffic versus ticket, grocery versus general merchandise, advertising, e-commerce profitability, inventory, and full-year guidance.
events.invalidation: A Walmart-specific result driven by share gains that does not match TGT, COST, HD, LOW, or consumer data.
events.watch: Retail breadth, XLY, and whether management describes resilient demand or broad trade-down behavior.

events.title: NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 financial results
events.implication: NVIDIA is the highest-information checkpoint for AI infrastructure demand, accelerator supply, networking, hyperscaler capex, sovereign AI, and the semiconductor complex.
events.direction: Bullish if data-center growth, gross margin, supply visibility, and forward demand beat elevated expectations; bearish if capacity, export controls, product transitions, or customer digestion weaken the outlook.
events.magnitude: The August 28 $205 call-plus-put marked about $23.20 at the July 24 close, implying roughly ±11.2% around a $206.80 after-hours stock mark. Indicative, not an executable fill.
events.action: Track data-center revenue, networking, gross margin, next-platform shipments, China/export commentary, and hyperscaler demand visibility.
events.invalidation: A large NVDA move that is driven by company-specific supply timing and does not confirm in AMD, AVGO, TSM, SMH, or QQQ.
events.watch: Semiconductor breadth and whether AI beneficiaries outside NVDA confirm the guidance signal.

events.title: Jackson Hole: Financial Innovation, Payments, and Policy
events.implication: The 2026 theme directly links monetary policy with payments and financial innovation. Central-bank language can move rates broadly and create specific read-throughs for banks, fintech, stablecoins, and crypto infrastructure.
events.direction: Hawkish policy language is bearish duration; constructive payments or innovation policy can support fintech and crypto, while restrictive language does the opposite.
events.magnitude: Speech-driven event; no defensible move estimate exists before the agenda and speakers are published.
events.action: Preload the agenda when released and prioritize speeches on inflation, payments, stablecoins, bank competition, and transmission of monetary policy.
events.invalidation: Academic discussion without new policy signals or market-moving central-bank guidance.
events.watch: 2-year yield, TLT, banks versus fintech, and COIN/PYPL/SQ reaction to payment-policy language.

events.title: August Employment Situation
events.implication: This closes the six-week window with a direct read on labor demand, wages, consumption capacity, and the path into the September FOMC meeting.
events.direction: Hot wages and payrolls can revive rate pressure; orderly cooling is supportive; abrupt deterioration is risk-off despite lower yields.
events.magnitude: Macro reaction only; no unsupported single-stock percentage is assigned.
events.action: Record payrolls, unemployment, wage growth, participation, and revisions, then separate the rates response from the growth response.
events.invalidation: A consensus-like release with small revisions and little bond-market movement.
events.watch: 2-year yield, TLT, QQQ versus XLF/XLY, and whether market breadth confirms the first move.

context: Selection is market-wide: events were ranked by expected index, sector, or cross-company information value—not by Bernard's holdings.
The scan covered confirmed high-market-cap earnings plus official Fed, BLS, company IR, and sector-policy calendars from July 25 through September 5, 2026.
Exact dates are separated from tentative dates. Tentative earnings were excluded from the top eight unless an official source corroborated them.
Option-implied ranges use July 24 closing marks on the first liquid expiration after each event and are labeled indicative.
methodology: Scan the full US-listed market over a rolling 42-day horizon. Rank catalysts by index weight, sector read-through, binary regulatory impact, breadth of affected tickers, and source confidence. Use primary-source dates first, verified earnings calendars second, and social/news only for discovery. Publish the eight highest-information events with bull/bear logic, measurable watch signals, and no portfolio bias.
